For \(x\in(\frac{\pi}{16},\frac{\pi}{8})\), the argument of cosine is
\[
\omega x+\frac{\pi}{4}\in \left(\frac{\omega\pi}{16}+\frac{\pi}{4},\ \frac{\omega\pi}{8}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right).
\]
We need this interval contained in some interval where \(\cos\le 0\):
\[
\left[\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi,\frac{3\pi}{2}+2k\pi\right].
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\omega\pi}{16}+\frac{\pi}{4}\ge \frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi
\]
and
\[
\frac{\omega\pi}{8}+\frac{\pi}{4}\le \frac{3\pi}{2}+2k\pi.
\]
Simplifying:
\[
\omega \ge 4+32k,\qquad \omega \le 10+16k.
\]
For an integer \(k\), the interval is nonempty when
\[
4+32k\le 10+16k \implies k\le 0.
\]
The maximum \(\omega\) occurs at the largest possible \(k=0\), giving
\[
\omega\le 10.
\]
Also \(\omega=10\) satisfies the conditions, so the maximum value is
\[
\boxed{10}.
\]
